The best Korean food, ever!
Dec 2017 • Couples
Recommended to try this place while we were in HCM. We didn’t regret a single bit. Everything was amazing, they refilled our side dishes and every single part of their dish was phenomenal.
Beef bulgogi and volcano fried rice. The whole experience of Korean BBQ is amazing, my fiancé who lived in Korea even said that Arirang was the best Korean bbq ever. The vegetables were fresh and crisp! Pork belly to bbq is highly recommended. I just couldn’t get enough of it. Right thickness, right taste(it is pretty weird, in Vietnam, pork usually smells and taste so weird but not in Arirang)
The portion is massive so make sure go easy on picking dishes cause you will be served plates of side dishes, that will be enough to fill you. 
The service was splendid, we were welcomed the moment we step our foot in their restaurant, everyone greeted us. The manager was full on with his service, he will be there and do his job to make sure customer go out of the restaurant satisfied with food and service. 
The servers know what they are doing, so efficient. They cooked the meat well as well. 
Everything was so perfect, alas, we managed to eat meat without costing so much. Most importantly, everything tastes like it is supposed to be. 
Lived in Singapore, lots of authentic Korean bbq but this by far, the best. They left a great impression of us. We love it!
I wish I could upload more photos but Tripadvisor being quite a pain to deal with.

Not my pick, but this was good stuff
Jun 2017 • Business
I normally wouldn't pick a restaurant that's not offering local food when I'm traveling, but since my Korean supplier brought me here and since I love Korean food I didn't say no. 
So taken that my primary choice of food in Vietnam would be Vietnamese I still had a great time enjoying good quality Korean food. The staff here is a mix of Korean and Vietnamese, but the food is purely Korean. We had some good quality meats with a selection of different types of leafs to wrap it in. My preference of choice is the nettles as they offer, in my view, the best complexity to the taste. 
At times the table was so full of dishes that some the plates were overlapping. 
There were elements, such as bok choi leaves for wrapping, that felt more local than Korean, but the quality of the food still kept pretty high standards to its intended cuisine.
